views.label: Electric Charge
views.settings: $r_s = 1$, the unit of every length, and $q = 2\,r_s$.
views.restriction: The plane of $t$ and $r$ with the circle of the fifth dimension divided out, each point in the diagram a 2-sphere times that circle. Light rays with no momentum along the circle run at 45 degrees.
caption: The electrically charged Kaluza-Klein black hole, maximally extended ($q = 2\,r_s$), with the circle of $y$ divided out, each point in the diagram a 2-sphere times that circle. The rays with no momentum along the circle keep $u$ or $v$, where $u, v = ct \mp r_*$ and the tortoise coordinate $r_*$ has $dr_*/dr = \sqrt{r(r + q - r_s)}/(r - r_s)$ and vanishes at $r = 0$. Kruskal's $U = -e^{-\kappa u}$ and $V = e^{\kappa v}$, with the surface gravity $\kappa = 1/(2\sqrt{q\,r_s})$, cross the horizon, and their arctangents put the singularity $r = 0$, where $UV = 1$, on the straight lines $T = \pm\pi/2$.

The coordinates $t$ and $r > r_s$ cover the right exterior. The horizon is the pair of null lines $U = 0$ and $V = 0$, crossing at the bifurcation surface, and the black hole above it ends at the spacelike singularity $r = 0$. The diagram is Schwarzschild's square for every charge, with no inner horizon.
legend: the exterior $r > r_s$, which $t$ and $r$ cover

views.label: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein
views.settings: $r_s = 1$, the unit of every length, and $q = 2\,r_s$.
views.restriction: The plane of $v$ and $r$ with the circle of the fifth dimension divided out, each point in the diagram a 2-sphere times that circle. Light rays with no momentum along the circle run at 45 degrees.
caption: The whole of the electrically charged hole ($q = 2\,r_s$) with the ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates $v$ and $r$ on it, the circle of $w$ divided out. They cover the exterior and the black hole together. An ingoing ray of the string's rest frame keeps $v$ and $w$ and so moves along the circle of $y$, and with the circle divided out its shadow, a line of constant $v$, is timelike.

views.label: Magnetic Charge
views.settings: $r_s = 1$, the unit of every length, and $p = 2\,r_s$.
views.restriction: The half axis $\theta = 0$ only, a totally geodesic surface, each point in the diagram a point of the axis times the circle of the fifth dimension.
caption: The magnetically charged Kaluza-Klein black hole, maximally extended ($p = 2\,r_s$), on its half axis $\theta = 0$, each point in the diagram a point of the axis times the circle of $y$. The metric on the plane of $t$ and $r$ is $(1 - r_s/r)(-c^2dt^2 + dr_*^2)$, where the tortoise coordinate $r_*$ has $dr_*/dr = \sqrt{r(r + p - r_s)}/(r - r_s)$, the electric hole's with $p$ in place of $q$, so the diagram is the same square.

The circle of $y$ shrinks toward the spacelike singularity $r = 0$, and on the horizon its circumference is $4\pi\sqrt{r_s(p - r_s)}$. At $r_s = 0$ the horizon and the singularity are gone, and the diagram is the triangle of the Kaluza-Klein monopole.
legend: the exterior $r > r_s$, which $t$ and $r$ cover

views.label: Equal Charges
views.settings: $r_s = 1$, the unit of every length, and $p = 3\,r_s$, so that $\rho_+ = 2\,r_s$ and $\rho_- = r_s$.
views.restriction: The plane of $t$ and $\rho$ with the circle of the fifth dimension divided out, each point in the diagram a 2-sphere times that circle. Light rays with no momentum along the circle run at 45 degrees.
caption: The Kaluza-Klein black hole of equal charges, maximally extended ($p = 3\,r_s$), with the circle of $y$ divided out, each point in the diagram a 2-sphere times that circle. The metric orthogonal to the circles is Reissner and Nordström's, with horizons at $\rho_\pm = (p \pm r_s)/2$, so the diagram is their tower: the exterior, the black hole between the horizons, and the region inside $\rho_-$, repeated without end.

The singularity $\rho = 0$ is timelike. The circle of the fifth dimension has one length everywhere, since the scalar field of four dimensions is constant when the charges are equal. At $r_s = 0$ the two horizons meet at $\rho = p/2$, an extremal hole whose horizon has the area $\pi p^2$.
legend: one exterior, one region between the horizons and one inside $\rho_-$, which $t$ and $\rho > 0$ cover
$\rho = 0$, a timelike singularity, where the Kretschmann scalar diverges

views.label: Einstein Metric, Four Dimensions
views.settings: $r_s = 1$, the unit of every length, and $q = 2\,r_s$.
caption: The Einstein metric of four dimensions of a Kaluza-Klein black hole of one charge, maximally extended ($q = 2\,r_s$), each point in the diagram a 2-sphere of area $4\pi r\sqrt{r(r + q - r_s)}$. It is $\sqrt{1 + (q - r_s)/r}$ times the metric orthogonal to the circles of the fifth dimension, and a conformal factor leaves every light ray where it is, so the diagram is the one drawn with the circle divided out.
The singularity $r = 0$ is spacelike, as Schwarzschild's is, and there is no inner horizon. At the extremal charge, $r_s = 0$, the horizon meets the singularity and its area is zero.
legend: the exterior $r > r_s$, which $t$ and $r$ cover

views.label: Einstein Metric, Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein
views.settings: $r_s = 1$, the unit of every length, and $q = 2\,r_s$.
caption: The whole of the Einstein metric of four dimensions ($q = 2\,r_s$) with its ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates $v$ and $r$ on it. They cover the exterior and the black hole together, and their lines of constant $v$ are ingoing light rays, which cross the horizon at 45° and end at $r = 0$.
